Listen to this article Share Pat Utomi, Professor of Political Economy, has warned that attempts to rig the 2027 general elections can plunge Nigeria into a severe national crisis, including a possible civil war, as concerns grow over the credibility of the forthcoming polls. Utomi spoke at a town hall meeting in Manchester, United Kingdom, where he said participants expressed concern over what they perceived as the confidence of some public officials that the outcome of the 2027 election was already predetermined. The political economist disclosed this in a post on X, explaining that he had attended a lunch to which Peter Obi, presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), was invited, but the gathering turned into a discussion about Nigeria’s political challenges. “I am in the middle of an accidental town hall meeting in Manchester in the UK. I came to a lunch to which Peter Obi was invited. I found food I looked forward to deferred for questions on the trouble with Nigeria,” Utomi wrote. He said participants were particularly troubled by what they considered the apparent determination of some politicians to manipulate the electoral process. “Many of the questions suggest worry about the boldness of public officials in projecting rigging with results of elections of 2027 considered in the pocket,” he said. “The determination to do whatever will prevent election malpractice suggests we may see a civil war if power tries to muscle the will of the people this time,” he added. According to Utomi, the participants also wanted to know how they could contribute to preventing electoral malpractice and protecting the integrity of the ballot. “They were energised to ask for how they could fight rigging,” he added. The professor warned that any attempt to subvert the will of voters could trigger devastating consequences for the country. Related News Otedola Bridge: How many more explosions before we act?
